title: Listing interop scenario playbook and copy sketch
content:
Purpose and scope:

This note is a compact playbook for partner listing interoperability scenarios and a scratchpad for marketplace tile and short-copy variants. It focuses on edge cases we repeatedly see during marketplace integrations (multi-cloud SKU mapping, private deployments, and billing fallbacks). Use as a preflight checklist for partner intake and as a canonical set of example copy snippets for tile teams to iterate from.

Intended audience: PMs, Partner Engineers, Technical Program Managers, and Listing Copywriters.

Quick summary of goals:
- Surface the cross-cloud interop scenarios that cause the most integration churn.
- Provide a minimal acceptance checklist partners must meet before publish.
- Offer tile/title/description copy variants (concise / technical / enterprise) for faster asset authoring.
- Enumerate telemetry and security gating items required for Dedicated/Private compatibility.

Top-level interoperability scenarios (high-value):
1) SKU parity and metering normalization (AWS/Azure/GCP)
   - Problem: partner-provided sku/usage units differ (tokens vs. API calls vs. embeddings units).
   - Acceptance: mapping table + sample invoice line item in vendor format.
   - Owner: Billing PM (Marcos Li)

2) Private deployment (VPC / on-prem) listing compatibility
   - Problem: Marketplace tiles assume cloud-managed entitlements but customer wants private control plane + KMS.
   - Acceptance: documented KEK/KMS flow, offline install artifact location, and an SSO entitlement flow.
   - Owner: Security/Private Deployments Eng (Nina Alvarez)

3) SSO + tenant provisioning flows (SCIM / SAML / OIDC)
   - Problem: marketplace provisioning sometimes uses an email invite flow; enterprise customers want SCIM provisioning + role sync.
   - Acceptance: SCIM endpoint, sample mapping payload, tenant lifecycle hooks for deprovision.
   - Owner: Partner Engineering (Elliot James)

4) Fallback model routing and SLA-compatible substitutions
   - Problem: partner listing references a model version unavailable in region; we require compatible fallback rules.
   - Acceptance: declare fallback model family, latency delta budget, and automated rollback triggers for quality regressions.
   - Owner: Product (hosted API)

Minimal preflight checklist (must pass all items or provide documented exceptions):
- [ ] SKU & metering mapping CSV attached to intake ticket (columns: vendor_sku, marketplace_sku, billing_unit, multiplier).
- [ ] Legal template (MSA + data processing addendum) reviewed and any redlines returned.
- [ ] Tile assets: logo (SVG 1x), hero PNG (1200x600), 30-word short description, 200-word long description, 3 bullets.
- [ ] Technical acceptance: smoke endpoint, healthz, telemetry event list, and documented throttling behavior.
- [ ] Security: required KMS/SAML/SCIM endpoints declared where relevant; network egress/IP ranges listed.
- [ ] QA plan: acceptance test list + rollback criteria + owner on-call for first 48h after publish.

Example tile copy (three flavors)
- Concise (launch tile):
  "Redwood Inference — High-performance LLM inference, hosted or private. Fast setup, predictable pricing."

- Technical (engineer-facing):
  "Serve LLMs at scale with Redwood Inference. Continuous batching, KV cache, and model-variant routing with observability into per-route latency and token cost."

- Enterprise (sales/ops):
  "Production-grade inference with dedicated and private deployment options, SLA-backed throughput, and KMS-integrated key management for regulated workloads."

30-word short description (example):
  "Low-latency LLM inference platform: hosted API, reserved GPU pools, and private deployment options with observability and cost controls for production applications."

3-bullet feature list (for tile bullets):
- "Hosted API + Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput"
- "Private deploy (VPC/on-prem) with KMS & audit logs"
- "Optimize tooling: batching, quantization, and cost-aware routing"

Acceptance test checklist (technical)
- Smoke endpoints: POST /v1/health (200), POST /v1/infer (sample request)
- Telemetry: emit events for request.received, request.latency_ms, billing.tokens_charged, auth.failure (list exact event names)
- Latency SLO demonstration: 95p token-latency under 500ms for a 512-token sequence in the representative region
- Rate limiting: documented 429 behavior and retry-after headers

Telemetry and observability requirements (short):
- Event spec (csv): event_name, required_fields, optional_fields, sample_payload
- Required events: request.start_ts, request.end_ts, model.variant, region, tokens.generated, billing.unit_count
- Correlation ID propagation: must accept x-request-id and echo in logs and telemetry

Compatibility matrix (CSV-style; small sample)
vendor,marketplace_sku,billing_unit,private_deploy_supported,notes
redwood-hosted,redwood-basic,tokens,false,hosted-only
redwood-dedicated,redwood-dedicated-hour,gpu-hours,true,requires-reserved-capacity
redwood-private,redwood-private-seat,seat,true,private install + KMS required

Security notes (minimum):
- KMS integration: document supported KMS providers + key rotation cadence.
- Network: list IP ranges for egress and control-plane (include CIDR).
- Data handling: confirm whether telemetry or logs contain PII and provide retention policy.

Edge-case playbook (short flows):
A) Model not available in requested region
  - If partner can provide model variant in that region -> proceed with region-specific tile variant.
  - Else auto-route to compatible fallback with downgrade notice and billing adjustment.
  - If neither available, mark tile as "region-limited" and prevent purchase flow in that region.

B) Customer requests private deployment but purchases via marketplace
  - Step 1: Auto-generate a "private-deploy request" ticket to partner-eng with order id.
  - Step 2: Ensure contract attachments (SLA, install window) are available before provisioning.

Rollback and incident runbook sketch (first 48h)
- Owner: partner-eng on-call -> respond within 30 minutes.
- Steps: 1) Identify offending release/tile change 2) Toggle marketplace routing to previous model variant 3) Pause new purchases 4) Notify customers via marketplace message 5) Create postmortem within 72 hours

Open questions / TODOs (please add answers in intake ticket JIRA-GTM-899):
- How do we represent consumption discounts for committed Dedicated capacity in marketplace billing lines? (pricing and invoicing model)
- Who signs the runbook for first-48h on-call across partner-eng and GTM Ops?
- Quick-UX question: Do we show "Private deployment available" as a badge or as a separate tile? Pros/cons noted in intake thread.

References and quick links:
- Confluence: CONF-4321 (marketplace integration playbook)
- Jira: JIRA-GTM-899 (this intake)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/marketplace/PR-214

Notes to self (writing style / reminders):
- Keep the short description under 30 words; avoid product rhetoric that conflicts with legal ("guaranteed" -> "SLA-backed" phrasing).
- When in doubt, prefer clarity for engineers: explicit endpoints, payloads, and sample JSON beats prose.
- Tag each tile asset with a version id (tile_v1, tile_v1_1) so we can roll forward/back easily.

Appendix: sample short FAQ snippets for marketplace support page
Q: Can I move from hosted to private?
A: Yes. Talk to partner-eng for a migration plan; data migration and KMS setup are required.

Q: What if a region runs out of capacity?
A: We will automatically offer a compatible variant or a queued provisioning window; enterprise customers can reserve Dedicated capacity to avoid this.

-- end of doc --
